data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Falsifiable-law candidate (deliberately minimal-commitment): whatever the limiting consensus probability is, the decisive quantity is the density of locally stable mixed configurations, and it obeys a clean quantitative law \u2014 the expected number of vertices that end in a dissenting matched pair after dynamics stabilizes scales like \u0398(n) with an explicit per-vertex constant \u03c1 \u2248 0.05\u20130.15 (empirically measurable), so the probability that this expected count is zero (i.e. consensus) converges to a Poisson-type limit: probability of consensus \u2192 exp(-\u03c1n) is ruled out; instead the count does not converge to a Poisson because the matching forms in correlated blocks, giving consensus probability tending to a constant strictly between 0 and 1 as n grows. The obstruction characterization: absorbing mixed states = colorings where every vertex agrees with two of its three neighbors, forcing the disagreeing-edge subgraph to be a matching whose removal leaves monochromatic induced components each of size \u2265 2.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the block-count actually converges to a Poisson distribution with mean growing or constant, the constant verdict changes (Poisson with constant mean would give consensus probability \u2192 e^{-\u03bb}, still strictly between 0 and 1 \u2014 this variant is admitted).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If measured \u03c1 = 0 for large n, consensus probability tends to 1.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If measured final dissenting count is o(n) but positive with constant probability, consensus probability tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1 via a different route.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Run the asynchronous dynamics: it reaches an absorbing state in O(n log n) steps whp because each unstable vertex flip strictly decreases the number of disagreeing edges when it had 2 or 3 disagreeing neighbors. The absorbing state's dissenting matching arises from blocks of vertices that were mutually reinforcing from time 0. Correlation between blocks decays with graph distance; on a locally tree-like random 3-regular graph, blocks behave roughly independently with constant per-vertex probability \u03c1 of harboring a final dissenting pair, so the total count is \u0398(n) (linear in n) with a law of large numbers rather than a Poisson limit; consensus requires all n blocks clean, a probability that is a nontrivial constant as n \u2192 \u221e because block correlations have global components (the final two basins compete), not independent multiplication.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
